title: A Unified Descriptive-Complexity Framework for Model Selection under Correlated Designs
abstract: arXiv:2608.26618v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Model selection becomes particularly challenging under strong predictor dependence and model-class uncertainty, especially when there are exponentially many models. We propose a Descriptive-Complexity Information Criterion (DCIC) that regularizes large candidate model collections through Kraft-admissible code lengths. Under sub-Weibull noise, we establish selection consistency through approximation-error separation without relying on RIP-type conditions, together with nonasymptotic oracle risk bounds that remain valid under model misspecification. The same coding principle places heterogeneous classes on a common complexity scale at a small additional class-identification cost. This extension yields class--model recovery under suitable identifiability conditions and risk adaptation across classes. translated_abstract: 摘要：在强预测变量依赖和模型类别不确定性下，模型选择变得尤为具有挑战性，尤其是当存在指数级数量的模型时。我们提出了一种描述复杂性信息准则（DCIC），通过Kraft可容许码长对大型候选模型集合进行正则化。在次Weibull噪声下，我们通过近似误差分离建立了选择一致性，无需依赖RIP型条件，同时获得了在模型误设下仍然有效的非渐近风险上界。相同的编码原则以较小的额外类别识别成本将异质类别置于共同的复杂性尺度上。这一扩展在适当的可识别性条件下实现了类别-模型恢复以及跨类别的风险自适应。我们进一步开发了一条复杂性引导的搜索路径，使计算-统计权衡变得明确。大惩罚产生多项式...（原文截断）
tldr: 本文提出一种统一的描述复杂性框架（DCIC），通过Kraft码长正则化在相关设计下实现模型选择一致性，并扩展至异质类别恢复，同时提供非渐近风险界和计算-统计权衡的显式路径。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a unified descriptive-complexity framework (DCIC) that regularizes model selection under correlated designs via Kraft-admissible code lengths, achieving selection consistency and heterogeneous class recovery with nonasymptotic risk bounds and explicit computation-statistics trade-offs.
